text:
support-ops: :rotating_light: Customer P96 is getting intermittent 502/504s and a bunch of 5xx gateway errors since ~09:10 UTC. They're hitting our hosted inference endpoint and timing out during bursts.
support-ops: We triaged logs — spikes align with other tenants experiencing high queue backpressure. Suspect autoscaler delay.
oncall-sre: Can you paste the gateway logs and any autoscaler events?
support-ops: Gateway snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T09:10:12Z gateway service request_id=abc123 upstream_timeout code=504 msg="upstream request timed out"
2026-03-17T09:10:13Z gateway service request_id=abc124 backend_error code=502 msg="no healthy upstream"
2026-03-17T09:11:05Z runner orchestration pod=runner-xxxxx status=Pending reason="WaitingForScaleUp"
```
support-ops: Autoscaler events show leader election flapping and long leader lock acquisitions: 
```
I0317 09:10:11.123456 1 leader_election.go:240] failed to acquire leader lease: timeout after 30s
I0317 09:10:42.654321 1 leader_election.go:180] acquired leader lease for duration 15s
```
oncall-sre: :eyes: That looks like lock contention. Are we seeing long GC pauses or etcd latency?
maria-g: Checking control-plane metrics — etcd_sd_rtt spiked to ~600ms around 09:09. kube-controller-manager leader election latencies also elevated.
kevin-p: Which autoscaler are these clusters using? HPA or our custom scaler?
support-ops: Hosted inference uses custom autoscaler with leader lock stored in redis (not etcd) for this fleet; we also run HPA as fallback in some zones. Logs above are from the custom scaler binary.
platform-joe: Redis slowlog shows blocking commands at the same time: multiple BLPOP operations waiting ~28s. Possible queue consumer backpressure causing the scaler to block while trying to acquire the lock.
sre-bot: Alert: multiple tenants reporting increased 95th latency for generate API; escalations: ticket#2345, ticket#2346.
customer-success-sam: Customer P96 reports repeated timeouts during a product demo, escalated to SE manager. Need ETA.
oncall-sre: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Release leader lock TTL to shorter value, 2) Force a new leader by restarting scaler pods in a rolling fashion, 3) Temporarily increase controller concurrency to accept more inflight scale requests. Which do we want to try?
maria-g: I recommend rolling restart of scaler pods in the affected region to break the stuck locks (do one at a time). Also increase redis maxclients and monitor.
kevin-p: Agreed. I'll start a rolling restart and bump redis client timeout. Commands: 
```
kubectl -n redwood-scalers rollout restart deployment/custom-autoscaler -l region=us-west-2
redis-cli -h redis-main SLOWLOG GET 10
```
platform-joe: Also enabling HPA fallback for the next 30m for the tenant's namespace to ensure we scale while lock churn stabilizes.
support-ops: Doing a coordinated ping with SE and P96. Notifying customer of workaround.
kevin-p: Rolling restart initiated. Watching events.
kevin-p: Event: scaler pod scaledown prevented due to PodDisruptionBudget, adjusting target to one-at-a-time.
maria-g: After first pod restart, leader election recovered and lock acquisition time dropped to <200ms. Gateway 5xx rate falling.
support-ops: Customer confirms reduced timeouts — demo resumed. :white_check_mark:
oncall-sre: Postmortem actions: - Migrate leader lock to ephemeral leader-election mechanism backed by etcd for faster TTLs - Add redis slowlog alerts and maxclients margin - Add automatic HPA fallback when scaler lock latency > 5s - Run chaos test for leader election under burst load
platform-joe: I'll open follow-up tickets and schedule a design review for moving to etcd-backed election.
customer-success-sam: I've updated the customer and closed the urgent ticket; they'll keep us posted if they see anything else.
support-ops: Thanks everyone. Closing incident when last 5xx rate < 1% for 15m.
